newsitem.title: INDIA: India state airlines to start code sharing.
newsitem.headline: India state airlines to start code sharing.

text.p: State-run Air India and Indian Airlines will start a code-sharing agreement on August 1, an senior Air India official said on Tuesday.
"The code-sharing agreement will come into effect from August 1, 1998," M.P. Mascarenhas, Air India's acting managing director, told Reuters after the company's board meeting.
The agreement will enable the two carriers to exchange a block of seats to accommodate each other's passengers.

Mascarenhas said the agreement marked the first phase of a pooling of resources between the two airlines, which currently operate under a common board. They have considered several options to join forces, including merger.
The board met on Tuesday to view a presentation on the pros and cons of a possible merger.
A senior Air India official, who asked not to be named, said that Air India was also negotiating a code sharing agreement with Continental Airlines Inc.
"This is an extension of our alliance with Air France, and would apply to our flights to and from the U.S.," the official said.
He added that negotiations were at a preliminary stage, and details were still to be worked out.
Air India and Air France announced a strategic alliance in May. Air France and Continental announced a similar agreement a month earlier.
Air India has similar agreements with Singapore Airlines Ltd, Scandinavian Airlines System and United Airlines.
